findings.reason: §2 and §5 should extend `node_probe` (or state why a second /proc reader in a second repo cannot be reused), which relocates where the node figures live and how §5 samples the fleet node.
findings.text: `read_host`/`read_cpu_times`/`read_meminfo` already read `/proc/stat` and `/proc/meminfo` and `NodeProbe.sample` (line 708) already samples them on cadence, so §2's node CPU/memory reads and §5's fleet-node sampling rebuild a mechanism imas-ambix already owns; the plan cites imas-ambix only for GPU figures

findings.reason: the plan should extend `locations.py`/`tunnel.py so one resolver serves services and the dashboard, instead of forking node resolution into a fourth reader.
findings.text: `_read_allocation_host`/`resolve_location` and `imas_codex/remote/tunnel.py:discover_compute_node` already own resolving "which compute node is that allocation on" from a scheduler query plus a recorded host, so §5's new fleet-node resolution in `host.py` is a third such path rather than an extension of the owner

findings.reason: naming one sampler owning the process table and exposing a small interface would stop the four sections from each walking `/proc` on a separate cadence, which is the incident's own failure mode (a monitor that repeats the load being watched).
findings.text: §2 (per-process CPU rate), §3 (owner census), §4 (orphan and long-running flags) and §6 (JSON-lines recorder) all iterate the same live process table and `/proc`, yet are described as four independent sections with no single collector module or interface, extending a module already dense with shallow `ps`/ssh wrappers

findings.reason: with this week's cli_options budget at 0, the section must account for the added surface in its own text, either by retiring an existing option/command or by stating why none can be.
findings.text: §6 adds the `imas-codex host report --since` command (a new CLI surface) and does not name what it retires or merges, nor why nothing can be

findings.reason: the plan should cite and mirror reckon's start-tick liveness reader (or state why a remote re-check cannot reuse it), so the identity re-check has one definition rather than two that can disagree.
findings.text: §4's `host kill` "re-checks that each still has the same start time and owner" before signalling, which is the pid-plus-recorded-start-tick liveness read reckon already owns (`record_process_alive` in `reckon/crew/runs.py`, used by `death_census`), and the plan does not name that owner for the re-check it calls for

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the plan adds per-process CPU rates, owner census, D-state sampling, orphan/long-running flags, a JSON-lines recorder and a report to `imas_codex/cli/host.py`, already 1788 lines of shallow ps/ssh helpers, with no stated sampler module or interface behind which that behaviour hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 adds a compute-node resolution path in `host.py` beside the existing resolver in `imas_codex/remote/tunnel.py` and `imas_codex/remote/locations.py`, which it does not extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 1 (`host report`, plan §6), mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §6 adds the `imas-codex host report` command without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites imas-ambix's serve recorder for GPU figures only, while `imas_ambix/agent/node_probe.py` already reads `/proc/stat` and `/proc/meminfo` for a node inside an allocation, which is the node CPU and memory figures §2 rebuilds and §5 samples.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the layers the plan adds over other owners name the machinery and justify reuse: §5 reads reckon's published reservation rather than a hard name, and §6 states it reads imas-ambix's recorder "instead of keeping a second scraper that can drift".
